tour.overview:
From 1802 to 1945, Hue was the capital of Vietnam under the thirteen emperors of the Nguyen dynasty. On the north bank of the Perfume River they built a walled citadel on the model of Beijing's Forbidden City, with a moat, palaces, temples and gardens, and in the hills upstream they designed elaborate tombs for themselves. Much of the citadel was destroyed in the battle of Hue in 1968; restoration continues. The Complex of Hue Monuments was Vietnam's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, in 1993.

This private day takes you from Hoi An or Da Nang to Hue and back with a licensed guide and a car, by way of the Hai Van Pass, one of the most beautiful coast roads in Asia. You explore the Imperial City, have a lunch of royal Hue cuisine, visit the tomb of Khai Dinh and end at the Thien Mu pagoda.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Hoi An or Da Nang
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; about 5 km with steps at the tomb

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Hai Van Pass and its old gate.
• Lang Co lagoon.
• The Imperial City, the Throne Palace and the Forbidden Purple City.
• The tomb of Khai Dinh.
• Thien Mu pagoda.

WHY THIS WORKS
Taking the pass rather than the tunnel adds the best views of the coast, and a private car makes a comfortable long day.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers and anyone based in Hoi An who wants to see Hue without moving hotel.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day near Hoi An, choose My Son or Ba Na Hills.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about three hours each way via the pass. Respectful dress is required at the pagoda and tombs. From October to December heavy rain and floods can affect the area.

days.name: The Hai Van Pass, Lang Co, the Imperial City, a royal lunch, the tomb of Khai Dinh and Thien Mu pagoda
days.description:
What to expect: the imperial capital of the Nguyen emperors and the coast road to reach it, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:00 and drive north along the coast past Da Nang to the Hai Van Pass, the 'pass of the ocean clouds', which crosses a spur of the Truong Son mountains running into the sea. At the top, 500 metres up, stands an old gate built by the emperors and the remains of French and American bunkers, with views back over Da Nang bay and forward over the lagoon of Lang Co, where you stop to see the fishing boats and oyster farms.

In Hue you enter the Imperial City through the Ngo Mon, the Noon Gate, used only by the emperor. Inside, you see the Thai Hoa Palace, the Hall of Supreme Harmony, where the emperors sat on their throne for great ceremonies, then the restored buildings and gardens of the Forbidden Purple City, once reserved for the emperor, his concubines and eunuchs, the long covered corridors, the theatre and the Mieu temple with its nine dynastic urns cast in bronze in the 1830s.

Lunch is a menu of Hue royal cuisine, small refined dishes once served at court, such as banh beo, steamed rice cakes, and the spicy beef noodle soup bun bo Hue. In the afternoon you drive into the hills to the tomb of Khai Dinh, the second-to-last emperor, built from 1920 to 1931 in a mix of Vietnamese and European styles: a long staircase lined with stone mandarins, elephants and horses leads to a concrete palace whose interior is covered in mosaics of glass and porcelain. You end at Thien Mu pagoda, whose seven-storey tower has stood on a hill above the Perfume River since 1844; the car in which the monk Thich Quang Duc drove to Saigon before his self-immolation in 1963 is kept there. You drive back over the pass or through the tunnel, arriving at about 19:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:00 – Hai Van Pass.
08:45 – Lang Co lagoon.
10:00 – Imperial City (about 2 hours).
12:15 – Royal-style lunch.
13:45 – Tomb of Khai Dinh.
15:00 – Thien Mu pagoda.
15:45 – Drive back.
19:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The tomb of Tu Duc or Minh Mang can replace or join Khai Dinh's.
• A dragon boat on the Perfume River can be added.
• Hue is often rainy from October to December.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Imperial City and tomb tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About three hours each way via the Hai Van Pass, or two and a half through the tunnel. We take the pass at least one way for the views.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Imperial City and the tomb of Khai Dinh. Thien Mu pagoda is free.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a menu of Hue royal cuisine. Vegetarian Hue cuisine, created by Buddhist monks, is excellent too.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who enjoy palaces and stories of emperors. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The Imperial City is flat but large; Khai Dinh's tomb has 127 steps.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight in Hue?
faq.answer: Yes, and it allows more tombs and a dragon-boat trip. We can book a hotel by the Perfume River.

faq.question: Can we ride the Hai Van Pass by motorbike?
faq.answer: Yes, with an experienced rider, as an option for part of the way; your car carries the luggage.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops at incense or conical-hat workshops unless you ask.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Covering clothes for temples and tombs, comfortable shoes and a light rain jacket in the rainy season.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: February to April is pleasant; May to August is hot and dry; September to December is rainy, with floods possible.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
